questions.question: What is the primary role of an API Gateway in a microservices architecture?

options.A: To store the application's primary database.
options.B: To act as a single entry point for all client requests and route them to the appropriate services.
options.C: To compile source code into executable files.
options.D: To provide a physical hardware firewall for the data center.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can handle cross-cutting concerns like authentication and SSL termination.
Which of the following are common features of an API Gateway? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Protocol Translation
options.D: Unit Testing

questions.question: What is 'Rate Limiting' in the context of an API Gateway?

options.A: Limiting the number of developers who can access the code.
options.B: Controlling the rate of traffic sent or received by a network interface or service to prevent abuse.
options.C: Reducing the speed of the internet connection.
options.D: Limiting the file size of API responses.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can be used to provide a unified interface for multiple different backend services.
Which of the following are popular API Gateway solutions? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Apigee
options.D: React

questions.question: What is 'Load Balancing' at the API Gateway level?

options.A: Ensuring the server has a balanced weight.
options.B: Distributing incoming API requests across multiple instances of a backend service to ensure high availability.
options.C: Balancing the number of GET and POST requests.
options.D: Formatting the JSON data to be symmetrical.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway is usually placed behind the backend microservices to protect them from the internal network.
Which security functions can an API Gateway perform? (Select all that apply)

options.C: DDoS Protection
options.D: Database Encryption

questions.question: What is 'Protocol Translation' (or Mediation)?

options.A: Translating the API documentation into different languages.
options.B: Converting a client's request from one protocol (e.g., HTTP) to another used by the backend (e.g., gRPC).
options.C: Changing the binary code of the server.
options.D: Updating the version of the API.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can help reduce latency by caching frequent API responses.
Which of these are valid 'Request Transformation' tasks? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Changing the body format (e.g., XML to JSON).
options.C: Renaming query parameters.
options.D: Deleting the original source code.

questions.question: What is a 'Circuit Breaker' pattern in a gateway environment?

options.A: A physical switch in the data center.
options.B: A mechanism that stops requests to a failing backend service to allow it to recover and prevent cascading failures.
options.C: A tool that deletes slow API keys.
options.D: A way to disconnect users with low credit scores.

questions.question: True or False: Using an API Gateway increases the attack surface of your application by adding an extra layer.

options.B: False (It reduces it by centralizing security and hiding backends)

questions.question: Which of the following are metrics an API Gateway typically monitors? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Throughput (Requests per second)
options.D: Total lines of code in the backend

questions.question: What is 'Service Discovery' in the context of an API Gateway?

options.A: Finding new APIs on the internet.
options.B: The process of automatically detecting the network locations (IP/Port) of microservice instances.
options.C: Searching for bugs in the code.
options.D: Naming the microservices correctly.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can serve as a central point for logging and auditing all external API traffic.

options.C: Backend service timeout.
options.D: Invalid JSON format.

options.A: Filter out sensitive data from the backend response.
options.B: Add custom headers for the client.
options.C: Aggregate data from multiple services into one response.
options.D: Change the backend's database password.

questions.question: True or False: A 'BFF' (Backend For Frontend) is a type of specialized API Gateway designed for a specific UI or device type.

options.B: Decrypting SSL-encrypted traffic at the gateway before sending it to backend services to reduce their processing load.
options.C: A way to block all secure traffic.
options.D: Updating the expiration date of a certificate.

questions.question: Which 'Target' types can an API Gateway route traffic to? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Virtual Machines (EC2/GCE)
options.D: Physical USB drives

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway should generally be stateless to facilitate easy scaling.
What is the primary risk of having a single API Gateway for an entire enterprise architecture?

options.B: It becomes a Single Point of Failure (SPOF) if not highly available.
options.C: It makes the APIs too fast.
options.D: It prevents developers from using Python.

questions.question: Which authentication methods can be offloaded to a gateway? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Basic Auth
options.D: Biometric scanning on the server

questions.question: True or False: API Monetization features allow a gateway to track usage and bill customers based on their API consumption.

options.A: A deployment that only happens in the morning.
options.B: Routing a small percentage of traffic to a new version of a service to test its stability before a full rollout.
options.C: Deleting the old version of a service immediately.
options.D: Using yellow icons in the dashboard.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Gateway Deployment' models? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Ingress Controller (Kubernetes)
options.D: Database Plugin

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can help with 'Versioning' by routing different URL paths (e.g., /v1 and /v2) to different service versions.

options.A: Combining multiple client requests into one.
options.B: The gateway calling multiple backend services to fulfill a single client request and merging the results.
options.C: Sorting requests by time.
options.D: Deleting duplicate requests.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of using an API Gateway? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Reducing the number of round-trips for the client.
options.D: Eliminating the need for backend code.

questions.question: True or False: 'Sticky Sessions' at the gateway level ensure that a client is always routed to the same backend instance.

options.B: An API object that manages external access to the services in a cluster, typically via HTTP.
options.C: The exit point of a cluster.
options.D: A tool for memory management.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a 'Forward Proxy' and an API Gateway (acting as a Reverse Proxy)?

options.A: A forward proxy sits in front of the client; a gateway sits in front of the backend services.
options.B: A gateway is only for mobile apps; a proxy is for browsers.
options.C: A forward proxy is hardware; a gateway is software.
options.D: There is no difference.

questions.question: True or False: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) policies can be managed centrally at the API Gateway level.
Which of these are valid methods for identifying a client at the Gateway for rate limiting? (Select all that apply)

options.C: OAuth2 Client ID
options.D: The user's monitor resolution

questions.question: Which HTTP status code is commonly returned by a Gateway when a backend service takes too long to respond?

options.C: 504 Gateway Timeout
options.D: 500 Internal Server Error

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can be configured to automatically retry a failed request to a backend service.
What are common ways to secure the communication between the Gateway and the Backend services? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Shared Secret Headers
options.D: Public DNS records

questions.question: What is 'IP Whitelisting'?

options.A: A list of IP addresses that are banned from the API.
options.B: A security configuration that only allows requests from a specific set of trusted IP addresses.
options.C: A way to hide the server's IP.
options.D: A list of websites the server can visit.

questions.question: True or False: The 'Host' header in an HTTP request is often used by the Gateway to determine which backend service to route the request to.
Which components are typically found in an API Management suite? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Analytics/Reporting Engine
options.D: IDE for writing Java code

questions.question: What is the purpose of an 'API Key'?

options.B: To identify and authorize the calling application or developer.
options.C: To unlock the server room door.
options.D: To speed up the internet connection.

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can modify the HTTP status code returned by the backend before it reaches the client.
Which of these are valid 'Caching' strategies for a Gateway? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Vary by Header (e.g., Cache by Accept-Language)
options.C: Manual cache invalidation via API call
options.D: Caching every POST request by default

options.A: Routing based on the physical path of the cables.
options.B: Routing requests to different backends based on the URL path (e.g., /users vs /orders).
options.C: Sorting files in the server folder.
options.D: A way to choose the shortest network route.

questions.question: True or False: If a Gateway fails, all traffic to the backend services it manages will be blocked unless there is a redundant Gateway in place.
Which protocols can a modern API Gateway handle? (Select all that apply)

options.C: gRPC
options.D: SMTP (for email sending only)

questions.question: What is the role of the 'Developer Portal' in API Management?

options.A: To host the actual API code.
options.B: To provide documentation, API key management, and self-service onboarding for external developers.
options.C: To act as a chat room for programmers.
options.D: To monitor server CPU usage.

questions.question: True or False: Serverless API Gateways (like AWS API Gateway) automatically scale the infrastructure based on the volume of incoming traffic.
Which of the following describes 'Request Mirroring' (or Shadowing)?

options.A: Copying the request to a second database.
options.B: Sending a copy of live traffic to a test service to observe performance without affecting the production response.
options.C: Flipping the JSON body vertically.
options.D: Synchronizing two different gateways.

questions.question: What are common 'Logging' details captured by a Gateway? (Select all that apply)

options.C: HTTP Method and Path
options.D: The backend developer's username

questions.question: True or False: An API Gateway can enforce a global 'Timeout' policy to ensure no client request hangs indefinitely.

options.A: Deleting the header of an HTML page.
options.B: Adding, modifying, or removing HTTP headers as the request/response passes through the gateway.
options.C: Changing the title of the API.
options.D: Formatting the code headers.

options.A: Checking if a JWT is expired
options.B: Verifying the 'scope' of an OAuth2 token
options.C: Checking a local blacklist for a specific user ID
options.D: Re-compiling the backend code

options.B: False (They still provide security, caching, and rate limiting)

questions.question: What is 'Query Parameter Mapping'?

options.A: Searching for parameters in a map.
options.B: Transforming the query parameters from the client request into a format the backend expects.
options.C: Deleting all query strings.
options.D: Using Google Maps in an API.

questions.question: Which of these are features of 'Apigee'? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Threat Protection
options.D: Physical Server Assembly

questions.question: True or False: The 'X-Forwarded-For' header is often added by the Gateway to inform the backend of the original client's IP address.

options.A: Routing based on the size of the images.
options.B: Routing requests to different services based on the actual content of the request body (e.g., an 'orderType' field).
options.C: Routing traffic to a content delivery network.
options.D: Sorting emails by subject.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Authentication' providers a Gateway can integrate with? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Active Directory / LDAP
options.D: The browser's bookmarks

options.A: The financial status of the company.
options.B: The health and availability of the gateway instances.
options.C: The mood of the developers.
options.D: The number of lines of code written today.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Gateway Configuration' formats? (Select all that apply)

options.C: Admin UI / Dashboard
options.D: Handwritten notes

options.D: A way to test the CSS of the page.

options.A: A single gateway used for all internal and external traffic.

options.A: Testing a new version of a service with production traffic without affecting users.
options.B: Profiling the performance of a new database schema under real load.
options.C: Synchronizing two production databases in real-time.
options.D: Debugging transient production issues without risk to the live response.

questions.question: True or False: In a 'Sidecar' proxy deployment (like Istio), each microservice instance has its own dedicated gateway proxy running alongside it.

options.B: To ensure both the Gateway and the Backend service authenticate each other via certificates.
options.C: To compress the data twice.
options.D: To allow the backend to skip the login check.

options.C: IP Hash
options.D: Random Walk
